vlm.identity_system_prompt:
Preserve speaker identity when constructing memory from the supplied character features.

- Voice features map exact IDs such as <voice_0> to timestamped transcripts. These IDs already identify the speakers; they remain usable even when no face features are supplied or the visible speaker cannot be identified.
- For every supplied voice ID with nonempty speech, include at least one episodic memory that quotes or faithfully summarizes that speaker's transcript, using the exact ID as the speaker. Preserve distinct substantive utterances as separate atomic memories. Do not replace the ID with 'a speaker', 'the voice track', or an inferred visual role.
- When a semantic conclusion concerns a known speaker, retain that speaker's exact voice ID. Use only IDs supplied in the input; do not copy example IDs from instructions.
- A voice ID does not establish which visible person is speaking. Do not assign it to the camera wearer or another visible person, or assert face/voice equivalence, without supporting evidence. If no face IDs are supplied, do not invent any.
- Keep dialogue grounded in the provided transcript. Do not substitute a plausible scene description for what the speaker actually said.

Keep the existing video_description/high_level_conclusions JSON schema and all other task instructions unchanged.

At 00:00, Speaker <voice_484> suggests that new participants should tell stories in front of the group to build familiarity.
At 00:05, Speaker <voice_1386> explains that self-introduction can earn a gift.
At 00:09, Speaker <voice_364> proposes hiding items inside the house, specifically mentioning coins.
At 00:11, Speaker <voice_500> assigns points or items, giving five to the first person and three to the second.
At 00:15, Speaker <voice_1049> confirms the arrangement.
At 00:21, Speaker <voice_1387> compares the activity to Easter-like traditions.
At 00:27, Speaker <voice_1388> reiterates the plan to hide coins and agrees.
Around 16.50s, a person wearing an orange shirt enters the room from the left.
The person in orange walks across the room, eventually standing near the balcony door.
The camera perspective shifts to show the legs of the person filming at 21.00s.
Towards the end, the person in orange stands still near the window, observing the room.
high_level_conclusions: The group is organizing a social activity that involves ice-breaking through storytelling and gift exchange.
There is a planned element of hiding items (coins) within the house, suggesting a scavenger hunt or treasure hunt.
The man in the white shirt appears to be the facilitator or host of the session.
The person in the orange shirt joins the group later, integrating into the ongoing activity.
The conversation indicates a casual, friendly atmosphere despite the structured rules being discussed.
